title: Rain Expected in Delhi-NCR After Heatwave - Udaipur Kiran
full_text:
New Delhi, September 11 (Udaipur Kiran) : After a sweltering heatwave, residents of Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) can look forward to some relief as the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts rainfall over the next few days. The weather has shifted dramatically in the past two days, with intense heat and humidity reminiscent of the summer months of June and July.
On September 11, the maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to reach 33 degrees Celsius, with a minimum of 26 degrees Celsius. Overcast skies are anticipated, along with the possibility of light rain.
Temperatures are projected to drop slightly on September 12, with a maximum of 31 degrees and a minimum of 25 degrees Celsius. Moderate rainfall is expected on this day. The forecast for September 13 indicates a maximum temperature of 32 degrees and a minimum of 26 degrees, accompanied by light rain.
The weather will remain similar on September 14, with temperatures ranging between 31 and 25 degrees Celsius. By September 15, the maximum temperature could fall to 31 degrees, while the minimum may drop to 24 degrees Celsius.
As the rain approaches, the air quality index (AQI) is also expected to improve. Currently, pollution levels in various areas of Delhi are categorized as moderate to poor. According to the Delhi Pollution Control Committee, the AQI readings vary across the city, with Anand Vihar at 80 (satisfactory) and Ashok Vihar at 139 (moderate).
In Noida, AQI levels are higher, with readings of 172 in Sector 125 and 163 in Sector 116. Meanwhile, Ghaziabad shows a mixed bag, with Govindpuram recording an AQI of 47 (good) and other areas like Indirapuram and Sanjay Nagar showing higher levels of pollution.
Residents of Delhi-NCR can expect a noticeable change in the weather over the next three days.
